definitions.explanation: A road designed specifically for motor vehicles, often a toll expressway with restricted access.

examples.japanese: {自動車道|じどうしゃどう}を{使|つか}えば{早|はや}く{着|つ}く。
examples.english: If you use the expressway, you'll arrive faster.

examples.japanese: {東名|とうめい}{自動車道|じどうしゃどう}は{東京|とうきょう}と{名古屋|なごや}を{結|むす}んでいる。
examples.english: The Tōmei Expressway connects Tokyo and Nagoya.

examples.japanese: お{盆|ぼん}の{時期|じき}は{自動車道|じどうしゃどう}が{渋滞|じゅうたい}するので{早|はや}めに{出発|しゅっぱつ}した{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: The expressways get congested during the Obon period, so it's better to leave early.

notes:
The formal name for major expressways in Japan. Many of Japan's expressways include {自動車道|じどうしゃどう} in their official names (e.g., {東名高速自動車道|とうめいこうそくじどうしゃどう}). In everyday speech, people often shorten these names or just say {高速|こうそく} (expressway) or {高速道路|こうそくどうろ}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高速|こうそく}{自動車道|じどうしゃどう} — high-speed expressway
- {自動車道|じどうしゃどう}の{料金|りょうきん} — expressway toll
- {自動車道|じどうしゃどう}の{出入|でい}り{口|ぐち} — expressway entrance/exit
- {自動車道|じどうしゃどう}が{渋滞|じゅうたい}する — the expressway is congested

RELATED WORDS:
- {高速道路|こうそくどうろ} — expressway, highway (more common in everyday speech)
- {国道|こくどう} — national highway
- {一般道|いっぱんどう} — regular road (as opposed to expressway)
